H200.summary: Multiple NVLink-connected GPUs—built for tightly coordinated work, with separate memory per GPU.
H200.goodFor: Large-model AI and FP64 scientific computation. On ICER’s compute nodes, NVLink lets GPUs exchange data efficiently when software distributes one job across them. Independent GPU jobs can run too.
H200.limitations: Not automatically one big GPU: each H200 has its own 141 GB memory pool. Software must explicitly distribute the work and data; allocating more GPUs alone does not combine their memory or speed up a program.

L40S.summary: Multiple independent GPUs—great for separate jobs; can also cooperate over PCIe.
L40S.goodFor: Separate GPU jobs, FP32 or mixed-precision AI, inference, and rendering. Multiple cards can also cooperate on one job through PCIe when supported by the software and system topology.
L40S.limitations: No NVLink: frequent cross-GPU communication can limit tightly coupled workloads. Each GPU has its own 48 GB memory pool. FP64-heavy solvers are a weaker fit; PCIe peer-access support must be verified rather than assuming every transfer is direct or always goes through CPU RAM.

A100.goodFor: Supported mixed-precision AI and FP64 scientific workloads.
A100.limitations: Memory is per GPU, not an automatically combined pool. ICER’s 80 GB SXM and 40 GB PCIe configurations differ in both capacity and NVLink connectivity.

V100S.goodFor: Compatible CUDA and FP64 scientific workloads that fit in 32 GB per GPU. Its 1134 GB/s peak local-memory bandwidth can help memory-bound calculations compared with V100’s 900 GB/s, without increasing memory capacity.
V100S.limitations: Not 26% faster for every application: that comparison is peak memory bandwidth, not measured application speed or GPU-to-GPU NVLink speed. ICER’s nvf nodes have mixed NVLink configurations; verify the allocated node.

V100.bandwidthComparison: V100S: 1134 GB/s, same 32 GB capacity here
V100.goodFor: Compatible CUDA and FP64 scientific workloads. ICER’s nvl nodes provide eight 32 GB V100 GPUs with NVLink; this can help explicitly coordinated multi-GPU jobs even though each GPU’s peak memory bandwidth is lower than V100S.
V100.limitations: Lower local-memory bandwidth than V100S: 900 versus 1134 GB/s per GPU. These are vendor peaks, not application or NVLink transfer speeds. Eight GPUs remain separate devices and do not automatically combine their memory.
